title: A household custom and care’s measure

captions.emotions: Feeling fairness in your shared work

meaning: A shared household custom supports you when growing care does not quietly make it more demanding for one of you.
text: Home can feel your own through familiar actions: knowing how to greet weekends, set the table and maintain usual routines. The Hierophant in the physical position of Muladhara describes participation in shared customs. The Empress in energy tests your footing through expanding care: preparing more, adding conveniences and looking after another detail. Justice in emotions notices the balance of effort. A warm tradition can therefore begin to feel different when its form grows without the time and work required becoming a subject of clear agreement.

For example, Sunday lunch began as one simple dish. Starters, dessert and compulsory attractive presentation have since joined it. **An expanded custom needs its care to be shared afresh.** The old name does not mean the old amount of work. Recognising the change need not surrender the pleasure of meeting at the table. The ritual can again express two people’s participation instead of testing someone’s readiness to do more unnoticed for a pleasant impression.

The difficulty is treating any reduction as insufficient generosity. Discussing workload then becomes an argument about who values family routines more. Fairness starts demanding exact accounts, and the familiar lunch loses warmth. A custom stays alive when it can return to a suitable size without dismissing work already given or the wish to care for each other.
